newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel gains on dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel gains on dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel representative rate was fixed higher against the dollar on Tuesday following the decline of the U.S. currency on overseas markets, dealers said.
"The lowering of the interest rate had no impact on trading today. The Bank of Israel had to intervene again, buying dollars to support the basket," said a dealer at Bank Hapoalim.
The Bank of Israel said on Monday, after the represenative rate had been set for the day, that it was lowering its key lending rate for March by 0.3 percentage point to an annualised 13.9 percent.

"The shekel rose slightly against the dollar because the U.S. currency declined on Monday after the rate was set," said the Hapoalim dealer. "In the near term the basket will remain under pressure because the business sector is continuing to take foreign currency-linked loans."

The central bank has been intervening regularly in the market to defend the currency basket rate, which has been trading at the bottom end of its band for more than a month. Traders estimated that the central bank bought over $100 million on Tuesday to support it.

The shekel is allowed to fluctuate in a band of seven percent above or below a sloping mid-point designed to devalue the Israeli currency at a rate of six percent a year against the basket of key currencies.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3390 shekels against 3.3420 on Monday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6411 shekels against 3.6407 on Monday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.7412 shekels per 100 yen against 2.7332 on Monday and against the mark at 1.9939 shekels against 1.9444 on Monday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.3390 shekels.
